comments.note: TaggerTagViewModel.OnIsCheckedStoredChanged is now fire-and-forget but exceptions are captured. If future work needs to surface structured errors (e.g., distinguish network vs. validation failures), ReportError could accept an Exception rather than a string. For now the message-only approach is sufficient.

The error bar in TaggerView.axaml uses hardcoded OrangeRed / #1FFF0000 colours. If a themed 'SystemFillColorCritical' brush is available via FluentAvalonia resources in future, replacing the literals would give better dark-mode contrast.

HasLastOperationError is raised via an explicit partial void OnLastOperationErrorChanged → OnPropertyChanged(nameof(HasLastOperationError)). An alternative is to use [NotifyPropertyChangedFor(nameof(HasLastOperationError))] on the _lastOperationError field, which is more idiomatic with CommunityToolkit.Mvvm and avoids the manual partial method.

comments.note: ExecuteToggleAsync is fire-and-forget and the _onError callback (which sets LastOperationError) may be invoked from a non-UI thread when real async DB callbacks complete. In tests this is safe because Task.FromException resolves synchronously. In production, if the DB callback completes on a thread-pool thread, the property change notification for LastOperationError could fire off-thread. Avalonia's ObservableObject does not automatically marshal to the UI thread. Consider wrapping the _onError callback invocation with Dispatcher.UIThread.Post if cross-thread issues arise in integration testing.

No test covers the implied-tag path (IsCheckedImplied=true → early return, error not cleared). This is intentional per spec but a test asserting that clicking an implied tag does not invoke _onError and does not clear an existing error would add confidence.

When RebuildCategories is called (e.g., via ITagsManager.DataChanged), LastOperationError on TaggerViewModel is NOT reset. A stale error message from a prior session remains visible until the next non-implied toggle. This is the documented 'persistent-until-cleared' pattern and is expected behavior, but it may surprise users if a DataChanged event fires after an error.

summary: [FAIL — Blocking] Cross-thread UI mutation in ExecuteToggleAsync. The catch block in TaggerTagViewModel.ExecuteToggleAsync invokes _onError?.Invoke(ex.Message) after ConfigureAwait(false), meaning LastOperationError is mutated on a thread-pool thread in production (real async DB callbacks). This is a threading bug introduced by WP-006: tests pass because Task.FromException resolves synchronously, but genuine async failures will invoke the error callback off the UI thread, risking Avalonia cross-thread binding violations. [Fix-Forward applied] Replaced partial void OnLastOperationErrorChanged with [NotifyPropertyChangedFor(nameof(HasLastOperationError))] attribute on _lastOperationError in TaggerViewModel.cs — more idiomatic CommunityToolkit.Mvvm pattern, non-behavioral.

comments.note: [BLOCKING] TaggerTagViewModel.ExecuteToggleAsync uses ConfigureAwait(false) and then invokes _onError?.Invoke(ex.Message) inside the catch block. In production, real async DB callbacks complete on thread-pool threads, so the catch continuation also runs on a thread-pool thread. This causes LastOperationError to be set from a non-UI thread, which fires INotifyPropertyChanged from a non-UI thread — a cross-thread access that Avalonia cannot guarantee to handle safely. Tests pass only because Task.FromException resolves synchronously during the await, keeping execution on the original UI thread. Fix: remove ConfigureAwait(false) from ExecuteToggleAsync (so the catch runs on the captured Avalonia SynchronizationContext), or wrap the _onError invocation with Avalonia.Threading.Dispatcher.UIThread.Post(...).

Applied Fix-Forward in TaggerViewModel.cs: removed the manual partial void OnLastOperationErrorChanged(string value) => OnPropertyChanged(nameof(HasLastOperationError)) and replaced it with the [NotifyPropertyChangedFor(nameof(HasLastOperationError))] attribute on the _lastOperationError field. This is the idiomatic CommunityToolkit.Mvvm pattern and produces equivalent source-generated code. Non-behavioral change — no test impact.

Minor suggestion for the Developer to apply during rework: the lambda onError: error => ReportError(error) in RebuildCategories can be simplified to the method group onError: ReportError. Non-behavioral — clean-up only.
